By contrast, LightMem reduces offline tokens through query-agnostic pre-compression, which can discard fine-grained details. APDMem offers a practical efficiency–accuracy trade-off: it avoids the high overhead of update-heavy systems while reducing reliance on aggressive compression, with minimal latency. (c) Error decomposition (retrieval vs. generation) for GPT-4.1-mini and GPT-4.1. 4.3 Effectiveness of Progressive Disclosure We analyze whether progressive disclosure achieves its design goal: locating relevant evidence with minimal memory access. Unless stated otherwise, statistics use the GPT-4.1 configuration; the error decomposition additionally contrasts GPT-4.1-mini with GPT-4.1 to study how backbone strength affects retrieval versus generation failures. Retrieval selectivity. Figure 2 (a) shows that the controller drills into only 8% of the haystack on average (3.7 out of 47.7 sessions per question). Single-session categories are the most selective (SS-Asst.: 2%, SS-User: 6%), while multi-session questions require broader access (12%). Despite this selectivity, APDMem achieves 87.8% overall accuracy, confirming that the Progressive Disclosure Controller enables precise evidence identification without exhaustive search. Disclosure depth distribution. Figure 2 (b) shows that the controller usually stops shallow: among 1,838 1{,}838 drills, 73.7% terminate at L 1 L_{1} , 20.2% descend to L 3 L_{3} , and 6.1% stop at L 2 L_{2} . Depth varies by question type: single-session queries use L 3 L_{3} most often (SS-Asst. 40.7%, SS-User 35.8%) because they often require exact phrasing, whereas multi-session and knowledge-update queries remain mostly shallow ( L 3 L_{3} rates of 15.2% and 9.9%). This demonstrates that the controller adapts disclosure depth to evidence demand rather than using a fixed retrieval granularity. Controller Generator Avg. Acc. Using gold session annotations, we classify predictions by Correct Retrieval and Correct Generation . Figure 2 (c) shows that scaling the backbone primarily reduces retrieval errors (22.2% → \to 10.6%), while generation errors remain near 8–10%, making evidence discovery the main bottleneck. This is confirmed by Table 3 : with the generator fixed to GPT-4.1-mini, upgrading only the controller raises accuracy from 79.8% to 86.8%, and a GPT-5.2 controller reaches 87.8%. Thus, APDMem enables heterogeneous deployment: when model budget is limited, capacity can be allocated to the controller, where the dominant bottleneck lies, while a lightweight model serves as the generator. 4.4 Ablation Studies We ablate three aspects of APDMem on GPT-4.1 in Table 4 : the controller, memory levels, and reasoning tools. To further disentangle the effect of hierarchical memory from agentic control, we additionally include a vanilla RAG ( L 3 L_{3} -only) baseline, which removes both the controller and the hierarchy and retrieves directly from raw messages. Case 1 answers a cross-session multi-hop question using only L 1 L_{1} facts, with reflect driving evidence-gathering and convergence. Case 2 answers a within-session verbatim question by descending the hierarchy from L 1 L_{1} to L 3 L_{3} . The two cases highlight the breadth-vs.-depth behavior enabled by the controller. Results. Three trends emerge, with drops reported relative to APDMem. (i) Controller and hierarchy : replacing the controller with a non-agentic RAG baseline while preserving the L 0 L_{0} – L 3 L_{3} hierarchy reduces accuracy from 87.8% to 83.2%, corresponding to a 5.2% relative drop. This shows that query-adaptive drilling and reflection add value over static retrieval. The vanilla RAG ( L 3 L_{3} -only) baseline further removes the hierarchy and retrieves only from raw messages ( L 3 L_{3} ), reducing accuracy to 77.0%, corresponding to a larger 12.3% relative drop. This comparison separates the contribution of the two components: the controller improves over hierarchical RAG, while the hierarchy itself provides a substantial gain over raw-message retrieval. (ii) Memory levels : key facts ( L 1 L_{1} , ↓ \downarrow 3.6%) and raw messages ( L 3 L_{3} , ↓ \downarrow 5.9%) cause the largest accuracy drops, consistent with APDMem’s broad-shallow and narrow-deep retrieval patterns. Turn-level evidence notes ( L 2 L_{2} , ↓ \downarrow 0.5%) have a smaller aggregate effect, serving primarily as an intermediate evidence layer. (iii) Reasoning tools : reflection contributes most ( ↓ \downarrow 3.6%), followed by decomposition ( ↓ \downarrow 2.1%); date interpretation has little effect ( ↓ \downarrow 0.2%), likely because the backbone model already handles many temporal cues. 4.5 Case Studies Figure 3 shows two representative LongMemEval traces illustrating how APDMem performs progressive disclosure in different scenarios.
